rationale: Standard Manichaean pair: ⲧⲱϩⲙ̄ (Call) sent by Living Spirit + ⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ (Hearing/Answer) from First Man. The two divinities added to the five elements yield seven (line 4).

Lyc. ⲡⲉϩ- 'his' + ⲱⲗⲏⲛ (root unidentified). Context — the Enemy and the release of captives — suggests combat semantics. May be Greek-derived (πόλεμος?) with elision of initial ⲡ-, or a Coptic verbal noun of carrying/bearing. Confidence low.
Compound place-noun ⲙⲁ- ('place') + unidentified element ⲍⲁⲓⲡⲧⲉ. Modified by ⲉⲧⲍⲏⲡ 'which is hidden.' Possibly a cosmic storehouse or treasury. Confidence low.

Lycopolitan plural of ⲓⲱⲧ/ⲉⲓⲱⲧ 'father' — the chapter that follows enumerates each Manichaean divine emanation as 'beginning' (ⲁⲣⲭⲏ) of a class of gifts. 'Fathers of the Light' fits the systematic enumeration: Father of Lights, Mother of Life (= foremost of Holy Spirit), Third Ambassador, Beloved of Lights, First Man.
Lyc. ⲱⲱⲡⲉ = ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'become.' Construction is the standard Coptic imperative-of-result: 'become you knowing' = 'know!' / 'be it known to you.' Standard Manichaean teacher-formula opening expositions.
Lyc. plural form, possibly from ⲱⲣϩ̄/ⲟⲩⲣϩ̄ 'guard, watcher.' Paired with ⲕⲩⲛⲏⲅⲟⲥ 'hunters' as classes deriving from the First Man. Confidence low.
Unidentified root, possibly Lyc. dialect form. Context (paired with hunters and watchers, all originating from First Man) supports a martial/combative class designation. Confidence low.
Lyc. = ϫⲱⲗϫ̄ 'fashion, prepare, mold.' Used in line 20 of those who fashioned the cosmos in the purpose of the heart.

proposed_english: the lower one / the lower place
rationale: Lyc. with demonstrative ⲡⲓ- + ⲧⲛⲉ (= ⲡⲉⲥⲏⲧ?). Spatial term for the lower cosmic register, contrasting with ⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ 'above.'
Abstract noun from ⲉϩⲧⲉ/ϩⲏⲧ 'front, before.' Repeated three times in lines 1, 7-8 designating the foremost place/rank of the Aeons or of blessing.
